instructions: Human-reviewed list used for the submitted report.

stakeholders.name: Dashcam owner / driver
stakeholders.description: Person who bought or was given the dashcam and whose car generates footage.
stakeholders.why_included: They control power, pairing, opt-in, and are the first privacy surface.

stakeholders.name: Missing child (search subject)
stakeholders.description: The child the authorized search is trying to locate.
stakeholders.why_included: The system's stated beneficiary; harms to them are the point of safety analysis.

stakeholders.name: Parent / guardian of the missing child
stakeholders.description: Family coordinating with the non-profit and authorities.
stakeholders.why_included: They live with false hope, delays, and leakage of family information.

stakeholders.name: Law enforcement / coordinating authorities
stakeholders.description: Officers and dispatchers who issue searches and act on sightings.
stakeholders.why_included: They are the actuator that turns a report into a real-world intervention.

stakeholders.name: Child-safety non-profit
stakeholders.description: Partner that coordinates searches and public trust around child recovery.
stakeholders.why_included: They hold the mission and the photo pipeline; a scandal ends the feature.

stakeholders.name: Automotive OEM
stakeholders.description: Car manufacturer that may factory-install the dashcam.
stakeholders.why_included: OEM contracts are the company's growth path and a vehicle-safety liability path.

stakeholders.name: Person-recognition contractor
stakeholders.description: Vendor that supplies and helps fine-tune the person/face recognition stack.
stakeholders.why_included: Their model is the ML component; their cloud/on-device choices change the threat model.

stakeholders.name: Bystander / other road user
stakeholders.description: Pedestrians, other drivers, and passengers whose faces appear in footage.
stakeholders.why_included: Most faces the model will ever see are not missing children; they bear biometric risk.

stakeholders.name: Innocent lookalike child and caregiver
stakeholders.description: A child or adult who resembles the search photo, and the adult with them.
stakeholders.why_included: False positives cause police contact, which is a different harm than a miss.

stakeholders.name: Privacy regulator / data-protection authority
stakeholders.description: Agency enforcing biometric, children's-data, and purpose-limitation rules.
stakeholders.why_included: Unlawful processing can shut the product down regardless of detection accuracy.

stakeholders.name: Gas-station / edge-kiosk partner
stakeholders.description: Business hosting drop-off or inference hardware that management wants to explore.
stakeholders.why_included: The scenario explicitly invites edge computing; it creates a new surveillance place.

stakeholders.name: Rideshare / fleet driver
stakeholders.description: Driver whose vehicle is a workplace and who may be required to keep the dashcam on.
stakeholders.why_included: Passengers did not buy the dashcam; employment pressure changes opt-in assumptions.
